title: Call: Iowa HSEMD Wants Declaration and Bag Request by 18:00

fields.systemName: Recorded Line - EOC Command Desk, Courthouse Annex

caller.name: HSEMD Regional Duty Officer
caller.label: Iowa Homeland Security and Emergency Management, Regional Duty Desk

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: Tallis EOC, this is the HSEMD regional duty officer. Is the Coordinator there? Good. I'll keep this quick. We have your noon product for Cedar Ford, CFDI4. Crest 23.4 feet at 06:00 Saturday, major flooding.

transcript.speaker: TCEMA
transcript.text: (Coordinator responds.)

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: Okay. The Governor's office is putting together a proclamation tonight for the Cedar basin counties. If Tallis wants in, I need your declaration request on my desk by 18:00. Not 18:30 when the next forecast comes out. 18:00.

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: Second thing. I need a WebEOC resource request for the 40,000 sandbags and the four 6-inch pumps. Every line needs the resource, the quantity, a delivery point and a needed-by time. If there's no delivery point and no time, it goes to the bottom of the pile. I have four other counties asking for the same pumps.

transcript.speaker: TCEMA
transcript.text: (Coordinator responds.)

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: Then put the real point on it. If it's the Levee Road staging site, say so, and give me a time you actually need them by. Not 'as soon as possible.' If the date has already passed, tell me that and mark it urgent. I'd rather know.

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: Third. Before I can put Tallis on the list for Guard sandbag crews, I need a written statement on the levee's condition from your Levee District. From the district itself, signed by the Superintendent. Not a line in your sitrep. Is the levee sound, is it seeping, where are the weak spots. Something I can hand up the chain.

transcript.speaker: TCEMA
transcript.text: (Coordinator responds.)

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: One more thing, a heads up. I just got off the phone with the Corps, Rock Island District levee safety. Their records show your Hollow Creek reach is about 1.1 feet lower than the rest of the crown. At 23.4 that leaves you about a foot and a half of freeboard there, against about 2.6 everywhere else. They can send a geotechnical engineer tomorrow morning, but only if someone asks. They're emailing your Superintendent now and copying your office.

transcript.speaker: TCEMA
transcript.text: (Coordinator responds.)

transcript.speaker: HSEMD
transcript.text: Send everything to dutyofficer@ia-hsemd.example and put it in WebEOC as well. The declaration request and the resource request by 18:00, and the levee statement as soon as the district can write it. If I don't hear from you by then, I'll assume Tallis is holding. Thanks.

voiceStyles.HSEMD: Man in his 50s, state duty officer, brisk and businesslike but not unfriendly, has several more calls to make, phones ringing faintly behind him

instructorNote: Main-storyline inject. Watch for three things. First, the Coordinator should submit the declaration request under EOP 6.6, because the forecast crest is at or above 23.0 ft. Second, the Coordinator should enter an ICS 213 through WebEOC for 40,000 bags and four 6-inch pumps, with Levee Road staging as the delivery point and a stated needed-by time. Because the 13.0 ft trigger has already passed, that request should be marked urgent. Third, the Levee Superintendent should give a candid written judgement of the levee condition, naming the Hollow Creek low spot and its reduced freeboard. The Superintendent should also request the USACE inspection through the EOC and put the low-spot sandbag cap first.
